title: MiTAC Unveils Liquid-Cooled, Open AI Infrastructure for Future-Proof Data Centers
summary: At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, MiTAC Computing Technology showcased its comprehensive suite of full-stack AI infrastructure. The company highlighted advanced liquid cooling and robust open platforms as crucial for scaling artificial intelligence operations efficiently and sustainably.
content:
San Jose, California – The relentless demands of artificial intelligence necessitate infrastructure that is powerful, efficient, and truly scalable. MiTAC Computing Technology seized the spotlight at the recent Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, showcasing a compelling suite of full-stack AI infrastructure. Under the theme "Scaling Open AI Infra with Full-Stack Innovation," MiTAC demonstrated how enterprises can harness AI’s immense potential, effectively addressing bottlenecks in traditional data center designs. The excitement around AI’s rapid acceleration highlighted the timeliness of MiTAC’s solutions.

At the core of MiTAC’s advanced offerings are two pivotal components: cutting-edge liquid cooling and robust open platforms. As AI workloads intensify and chip densities soar, conventional air cooling frequently falls short, leading to inefficiencies and performance limits. MiTAC’s strong emphasis on liquid cooling directly confronts these challenges, promising superior thermal management, significant operational cost reductions, and the ability to integrate greater computational power. This isn't merely about heat mitigation; it’s about unleashing sustained peak performance for demanding AI tasks.

Equally critical is their unwavering commitment to open platforms. In an industry often constrained by proprietary systems, MiTAC’s dedication to open standards aligns perfectly with the OCP’s foundational ethos. These platforms provide essential flexibility and interoperability for businesses to construct agile, future-proof AI environments. By embracing open hardware and software, organizations can bypass vendor lock-in, accelerate innovation, and optimize infrastructure for diverse AI applications. This comprehensive strategy positions MiTAC as a key enabler for next-generation AI deployment.

MiTAC’s presence at the OCP Global Summit was more than an exhibition; it was a clear articulation of their strategic vision for AI’s future. They are delivering a holistic ecosystem engineered to meet the extreme performance and efficiency demands of modern AI. Their pioneering work in liquid cooling and dedication to open architectures are poised to fundamentally reshape how organizations deploy and scale AI, making high-performance computing both more accessible and sustainable. This pragmatic approach is vital for an industry constantly pushing boundaries.
keyTakeaways: MiTAC unveiled a comprehensive full-stack AI infrastructure suite at the OCP Global Summit.
Their solutions prominently feature advanced liquid cooling for enhanced thermal management and efficiency in high-density AI environments.
MiTAC champions open platforms to foster flexibility, interoperability, and accelerated innovation in AI infrastructure development.
author: Yunnie Cheng

title: Journalistic Firestorm: Trump-Linked VC Firm Weighs Legal Action Against ABC News
summary: A venture capital firm with ties to Donald Trump Jr., 1789 Capital, is considering legal action against ABC News following the network's deletion and revision of a report concerning the Trump family. The firm's attorneys are in communication with ABC News and Disney, signaling potential significant consequences for the broadcaster over the "botched report."
content:
A significant media showdown is brewing, with ABC News potentially facing severe legal repercussions. 1789 Capital, a venture capital firm notable for its connections to Donald Trump Jr., is actively considering a lawsuit against the broadcasting giant. This comes after ABC News recently retracted and substantially revised a report that apparently touched upon the Trump family, prompting accusations of a "botched" journalistic effort.

The dispute centers on a report, the specifics of which remain somewhat veiled but clearly triggered a strong reaction from 1789 Capital. The firm alleges that ABC's initial reporting was so flawed it necessitated a complete deletion and subsequent revision, a move that rarely goes unnoticed in the highly scrutinized world of major news media. "We still have our attorneys completely plugged into everything," a representative from 1789 Capital stated, signaling their determination to pursue all available avenues.

For ABC News, the situation presents a serious challenge to its journalistic credibility. Retractions and revisions, particularly those leading to legal threats, are black eyes for any news organization, raising questions about internal fact-checking processes and editorial oversight. Given the politically charged landscape surrounding the Trump family, any perceived misstep by a major media outlet is magnified, inviting intense scrutiny from all sides. The firm's direct engagement with ABC News and its parent company, Disney, underscores the seriousness of their intent and the potential financial and reputational stakes involved.

The unfolding saga highlights the razor-thin margin for error in contemporary journalism and the growing assertiveness of subjects willing to challenge what they deem inaccurate reporting. As 1789 Capital’s legal team continues its discussions, the industry watches closely to see if this disagreement escalates into a full-blown court battle, setting a precedent for how major news organizations handle public apologies and alleged damages in an increasingly litigious environment.
keyTakeaways: 1789 Capital, a venture capital firm linked to Donald Trump Jr., is contemplating legal action against ABC News.
The potential lawsuit stems from ABC News deleting and revising a report deemed "botched" by 1789 Capital.
The dispute raises significant questions about journalistic standards, media credibility, and the legal repercussions for major news organizations.
author: Staff Writer
